top_story: Iran’s internal strain is sharpening as Narges Mohammadi lies in critical condition after her transfer from prison to a cardiac unit in northwestern Iran, reinforcing the regime’s readiness to absorb domestic human costs while confronting external pressure. Since Trump’s March threat to destroy Iranian power infrastructure unless Tehran reopened the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian officials have framed any US military role there as grounds for regional escalation. That line hardened on 3–4 May, moving from warnings that US escorts would violate the ceasefire to an explicit threat to attack American forces entering the strait. The convergence of domestic repression and escalating brinkmanship suggests Tehran is tightening coercive control at home while raising the risk of a direct Gulf confrontation abroad.
